tools.name: render_pdf
tools.description: Lays out a whole HTML document (with its CSS) as paged print and returns a download link to the PDF, valid 24 hours, and the document's edit link in the ReflowPDF editor. Use @page for paper and margins, margin boxes for headers, footers and page numbers; JavaScript does not run. Read read_guide top

tools.name: render_template
tools.description: Fills a template with JSON data and prints it to PDF (a download link, valid 24 hours, and the edit link in the editor, where its template and data stay editable — until the person edits it on the page, which makes it a plain HTML document: then change its html). tools.name: list_templates
tools.description: Lists the gallery's ready documents — invoices, quotes, receipts, statements, reports, contracts, letters, CVs, certificates, tickets, labels, menus and more — each a template with sample data. Search by a word ("invoice", "contract") or a category.

tools.name: get_template
tools.description: Returns a gallery template's source and its sample data, to fill with the person's values (render_template) or to adapt into your own template.

tools.name: open_in_editor
tools.description: Returns the edit link of a document in the ReflowPDF editor, where the person edits it on the page and downloads it: your HTML, or a template with its data (kept as template and data, both editable). Use when the person wants to change the document themselves; you can read their changes and change i

tools.name: get_document
tools.description: Returns a document made with ReflowPDF (by you, or opened in the editor from your link) as it is now — the person may have edited it in the editor: its source HTML, template data and revision. Read it before changing it with update_document.

tools.name: update_document
tools.description: Writes a new version of a document by its link — e.g. the person asks in the chat to remove something on page 2 — and prints it again: the PDF link, the same edit link (the editor open on it shows the change). findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: render_pdf, list_templates, open_in_editor, get_document, update_document, upload_image, ask_for_images, read_guide · Private data: render_pdf, render_template, list_templates, open_in_editor, get_document, update_document, upload_image, ask_for_images, import_pdf, connect_account · Public sink: render_template, update_document, upload_image, ask_for_images · Destructive: render_pdf, update_document, read_guide.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: render_pdf, list_templates, open_in_editor, get_document, update_document, upload_image, ask_for_images, read_guide · Private data: render_pdf, render_template, list_templates, open_in_editor, get_document, update_document, upload_image, ask_for_images, import_pdf, connect_account · Public sink: render_template, update_document, upload_image, ask_for_images · Destructive: render_pdf, update_document, read_guide

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
